model_contribution.note: A negative false_positive_rate_delta is the win worth having: on this corpus the rules catch almost every attack and hold most of the clean traffic, so the model layer is judged on whether it releases honest shipments without releasing attacks.

hs_classification.note: `holdout` substitutions are absent from data/hs_reference.yaml. Recall there is the number that says whether the reference table generalises; `pairs` was tuned against.

adjacent_hs_negatives.note: Benign goods declared under the heading an evader would use as cover. An HS mismatch claimed here is the classifier learning the cover heading rather than the goods.

zero_day.measurement_limit: Stubbed searches return an EMPTY result, never a fabricated adverse finding -- inventing news would feed the corpus labels to the model through the tool and then grade it on repeating them. So adverse-media DETECTION is measured only on the --real-tavily subset; the rest measures the gate and the model's handling of absence. Tavily's free tier is 1,000 credits a month, which is why the subset exists.

notes: Rules plus the HS classifier (Nemotron Nano, cot_strict) plus the zero-day radar, through the real gate. 200 holdout cases by stride.
Adverse-media detection is measured on the 9 cases that used a real Tavily search; the rest used an empty stub, never a fabricated result.
The model layer added 2 false positives, both an HS mismatch claimed against a non-controlled heading (floor 40), and caught the 7 HS substitutions the tuned rules alone missed.
